description.narrative:
Det övergripande syftet med insatsen är att förbättra levnadsvillkoren för befolkningen på landsbygden med speciellt fokus på kvinnor och minska fattigdomen i denna målgrupp genom: 1) Ökad inkomst för små lantbrukare 2) Ökad resiliens i produktionen för småskaliga lantbrukare mot klimatförändringar 3) Förbättrade arbetsvillkor för män och kvinnor för minskad social sårbarhet 4) Ökad kvinnlig egenmakt 5) Förbättrat deltagande i publik planering och styrandemekanismer
Insatsen är ett samarbete mellan Schweiziska utvecklings institutionen (SDC) och Sveriges Ambassad i Bolivia (härefter "Ambassaden") där genomförandeparten är Swisscontakt, en global NGO med kontor i La Paz. Insatsen baseras på habilitering och koordinering av aktiviteter där olika marknadsaktörer ger människor på landsbygden, med fokus på kvinnor, ökad tillgång till finansiella och icke finansiella tjänster, teknik och service. Aktiviteterna väntas bidra till ökad inkomst framförallt i försäljning av livsmedel, främjandet av miljövänliga marknadsmodeller (såsom ekologiska produkter och hållbara produktionssystem) och en ökad ekonomisk, social och miljömässig resiliens.
I utvecklandet av programmet och analys av kontext har Swisscontakt tillsammans med Svenska Ambassaden arbetat med den multidimensionella fattigdomsanalysen (MDPA) tillsammans med en "Market for the poor" (M4P) ansats och dessa två ansatser kombinerade kommer att genomsyra genomförandet av insatsen.

The main objective of the project is to improve the living conditions of the target population and thereby reducing their levels of poverty. Specific objectives of the project are to: i) increase the net incomes of productive family units, ii) increase their resilience towards climate change, iii) improve their working conditions (employment/self-employment), and reducing their social vulnerability, iv) enhance the empowerment of women, and v) improve participatory public planning and management mechanisms.
The Project will have five planned components: - Development and access to product markets - Development and access to non-financial services markets, inputs and technologies - Development and access to financial products and services - Favorable context for social and economic development - Women´s empowerment
The contribution is a co-financed between The Swedish Embassy in La Paz (The Embassy) and the Swiss Development Cooperation in Bolivia and the implementing partner is Swisscontact, a global NGO with three offices in Bolivia.
The intervention is based on the facilitation of coordinated actions where the different system markets actors can bring financial and non-financial services, supplies, technology in accessible and inclusive conditions to rural families (with emphasis on women). Those interventions should allow more and better incomes for the sales of their products in a more environmental friendly business model, lowering at the same time their risk. Swisscontact has together with The Embassy been using the multidimensional poverty analysis approach combined with the markets for the poor approach in the development of the programme and in the analysis of context and identification of target groups. These two approaches will be implemented throughout the programme.

The main objective of the project is to improve the living conditions of the target population and thereby reducing their levels of poverty contributing mainly to SDG 1. Specific objectives of the project are to: - i) increase the net incomes of productive family units, - ii) increase their resilience towards climate change, - iii) improve their working conditions (employment/self-employment), and reducing their social vulnerability, - iv) enhance the empowerment of women, and - v) improve participatory public planning and management mechanisms. The intended outcome are: - 27.000 Small Farmers will get access to services, resources and markets in a favourable environment - 16.000 Small Farmers will increase Productivity and Employment - 10.000 Small Farmers will rise their Net Incomes more that 30% In all cases an analysis of men and women´s participation will be done. For achieving the goals proposed for the project, five components have been established: - Component 1 Development and access to product markets - Component 2 Development and access to non-financial services markets, inputs and technologies - Component 3 Development and access to financial products and services - Component 4 Favourable context for social and economic development - Component 5 Women's empowerment Additional comments for the 3rd amendment of the programme: The overall objective of the intervention will not change, but the environmental focus will be further strenghtened. Especially the added part of the intervention focusing on reforestation will hopefully have long term positive effects on the target group, since apart from decreasing greenhouse gases it will provide better farming opportunities on the high plateau of Bolivia.

The project has contributed to "Reducing poverty and improving the quality of life of rural families in prioritized territories", by helping Farming Production Units (Unidades Productivas Familiares - UPF) increase their net income and improve conditions for self-employment; increase agricultural productivity, reduce costs, and improve marketing conditions for their products. During its implementation it has adopted three approaches with a view at achieving the sustainability and efficiency of initiatives: i) Inclusive Market Systems Development Approach, promoting the articulation of actors and facilitation efforts to achieve changes in market systems, ii) Multidimensional Poverty Approach, that allows identifying actions in other dimensions of poverty beyond the purely economic one (human security, power and voice, opportunity and choice), and iii) Gender Approach.
During the whole intervention (2018-2021), 31,000 thousand men and women, heads of Farming Production Units had access to the goods and services provided by the project, of this number, 51% are women.
More than 13,000 Farming Production Units increased their net income by an average of 211% compared to a comparison group (206 USD/year increase on average). These beneficiaries correspond to productive complexes of economic importance (fruit trees, vegetables, tubers and quinoa) in the departments of La Paz, Oruro and Potosí.
Higher net income and the sustainability strategies projects interventions significantly helped 27,814 women and men to improve the working conditions (self-employment) of their small landholdings. 10,702 Farming production units have improved their climate change adaptation strategies, through the use of bio-inputs, preventive management of pests and diseases, use short-cycle and certified seed, and the adoption of technology and good practices (including climate forecast services, reliable early warnings and efficient use of water for irrigation) and 8,652 women expanded and improved their empowerment capacities.
On the other hand, it is important to mention that the program has been able to introduce a climate resilience approach not only at the local level but also at the national one. Among the main results it can be mentioned:
- Successful pilot experiences for potato and quinoa. The promotion of short-cycle product varieties contributes to increase yields by up to 30% and 10% higher sales price for potatoes, and to reduce losses by up to 33% for quinoa. The experience has been adopted by public entities (INIAF and municipal governments) and private entities (three producers associations of seed growers and seven input suppliers). - Four plant health municipal laws (out of 7 that have been prepared) to mainstream and fund integrated pest management actions at local levels have been approved (plant health is one of the main tools to combat the effects of climate change due to its effects in reducing losses of up to 20% in different crops). - A Training Program for Community Facilitators in Irrigation (SENARI - MMAyA) carried out by the National School of Irrigation has been implemented -A pilot meteorological information and weather forecasting and early warning services incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) of local producers in the valleys of La Paz tested (it has shown positive effects in reducing irrigation frequency for leafy vegetables and, therefore, reduced water uses and production costs. This experience is being replied in the Altiplano region). - A specific livestock insurance developed for dairy and dual-purpose cattle, with direct effects on the economic resilience of the small landholdings when herds are affected by climate change (lightning, frost, hail, snowfall and floods). Insured amount reached Bs 350,500 (321 head of cattle) - Development of innovations on a commercial scale to expand agroecological farming, which includes bio-inputs, soil recovery strategies and the efficient use of water. - Reforestation efforts to protect water sources resulted in 38,164 trees planted in Oruro and Cochabamba regions. It has been possible to fix 345.5t of total CO2 until December 2021 in the planted area (38 hectares).
The main results per components are as follow.
Component 1 Development and Access to Product Markets.
Up to 1,348 Farming Production Units supply products demanded in international markets to intermediaries and/or private export companies. 1,795 small landholdings sell their products to new markets, through innovative marketing channels. It has been possible to exceed the goals of the phase in this component by 134% and 119%. The facilitation actions made it possible for market actors to create 3 commercial articulation mechanisms and for 8 companies and other organizations (industries, marketers, state institutions, among others) to demand improved products of Farming Production Units, directly or through other actors. The export promotion actions, implemented in coordination with OTGS have introduced Bolivian products in the Scandinavian market. Ambassador Shop mechanism for the export of Bolivian products to Scandinavia have been implemented, and the construction of a sectoral brand for the Swedish market called Conscious foods from Bolivia.
Component 2 Development and Access to Services, Inputs and Technologies Markets.
The project has made possible for 31,137 UPF (15,904 women, 51% of the total) to access more and better services, technologies and supplies in 3 departments and 30 municipalities, exceeding the goal of the phase by 155%. The facilitation actions made it possible for 26 providers (18 public and 8 private) to provide services (advice, technical assistance, and training) under different schemes, strategies and coverage. Currently, 6 associations and 3 seed companies offer quality seed and technical assistance to potato and quinoa producers. Likewise, 10 suppliers (agricultural) offer inputs with information and advice and some of them market bio-inputs. 16 suppliers have been strengthened and articulated to offer technologies related to agricultural production, access and use of water, soil management and others appropriate to the characteristics of small-scale agriculture, especially for women.
Component 3 Development and Access to Financial Products and Services.
The intervention has supported 4,499 Farming Production Units to access financing under better conditions to invest in their agricultural production activity. It has helped 7,023 people to access insurance products (livestock insurance, life/burial insurance, and COVID insurance), thus exceeding the phase goals by 12% and 75%, respectively.
It has also enabled five financial service providers to offer more and better products and/or services suited to the conditions and needs of farming production units (especially the needs of women), so that they can invest in their agricultural economic activities (irrigation systems etc..). Seven insurance/microinsurance providers offer products appropriate to the characteristics and needs of the UPF. It is important to mention from a multidimensional poverty perspective, that the life and accident microinsurance provided by the project falls within the Human Security Dimension, since the farmer can transfer the risks of an adverse event to an insurance company and thus improve their safety and resilience, with the participation of insurance companies and support institutions (associations, private and public companies).
Also, coordinated work with financial institutions has allowed 15,466 UPF to access financial education services provided through face-to-face, virtual and radio broadcast workshops. During the pandemic, technology has been introduced to Financial Education through EDUFINA, a mobile application that allows self-learning in financial matters, available in native languages such as Quechua and Aymara, which has facilitated this process.
Component 4 Favourable Socio-Economic Environment.
All actions implemented by the project to improve the rural economic and social environment have been built on a basis to create synergies at all public levels. The improved public services as a result of the strengthening of institutional capacities and the provision of new public management instruments focused both at the thematic level, through alliances with the National Irrigation Service - SENARI (irrigation water management), the Unit of Complementary School Feeding of the GAM La Paz - UNACE (healthy nutrition) and the State Service of Autonomies - SEA (autonomous management for productive development), and also transversally, via the Federation of Municipal Associations of Bolivia - FAM Bolivia, among others.
The alliance with SENARI resulted in seven versions of the Community Irrigation Facilitators Program, certified by the Ministry of Education. At the basic technical level, a total of 254 technicians and irrigators were certified, in 7 versions of the program (Oruro (3), La Paz (1), Chuquisaca (1) and Potosí (2)). Likewise, at the auxiliary technical level (immediately above the Basic Technician), two versions of the program were completed (Oruro (1) and Potosí (1)), with a total of 106 participants and, of these, 79 participants certified. Also, 16 short specialization courses were held in a variety of topics related to irrigation water management, with the participation of 816 professionals (578 men and 238 women).
Autonomous public management was strengthened through support for the drafting and publication of three municipal guidelines (two methodological guidelines and a regulatory one) by the State Service of Autonomies SEA, to guide development of municipal policies, programs and projects on issues of agriculture production and promoting economic recovery after the pandemic.
The municipal associative system was also supported through strengthening actions with FAM. During the pandemic, alternative strategies to sell local production, mainly rural, were developed through the development of a Family Farming Production Platform (Alimentar Bolivia). This initiative involved 330 producers of 21 municipalities, mainly of the La Paz, Cochabamba and Santa Cruz regions. It is expected that a second phase will be managed by the FAM.
Component 5 Empowering women.
The project highlights the implementation of schemes to strengthen Municipal Comprehensive Legal Services (SLIM) to manage violence against women, together with two public universities: Universidad Mayor de San Andres and Universidad Técnica de Oruro. Formal agreements were reached and mainstreamed in both cases through a formal commitment of the relevant authorities and formal staffing for the model/program.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
